images.title: A scale with a needle past 3 kg
images.purpose: Show how to read a scale with a needle: start at 0, find the last label passed (3 kg), then count the marks after it (3 marks of 200 g).
images.composition: One large round scale in the middle with the needle between the 3 kg and 4 kg labels and the reading in a box below.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. DIAL: a circle centred at (728, 380), radius 250 px, outline 8 px dark #1F2937, filled white. Hub: a circle of radius 16 px at the centre filled teal #0072B2. MARKS: exactly 25 small radial marks, one every 14.4 degrees clockwise from the top, mark 0 at the top. The 5 long marks (44 px long, 6 px thick, dark #1F2937) are marks 0, 5, 10, 15, 20; every other mark is short (24 px long, 3 px thick, grey #6B7280). The marks run inward from radius 242. LABELS (centred on the point, 36 px, bold; the 0 is reddish purple #CC79A7, all others dark #1F2937): 0 at (728, 208); 1 kg at (892, 327); 2 kg at (829, 519); 3 kg at (627, 519); 4 kg at (564, 327). NEEDLE: one straight needle from the hub to (527, 418), which is on mark 18 (259.2 degrees clockwise from the top), 9 px thick, amber #E69F00, ending in a small triangle arrowhead 26 px long; nothing else crosses it. READING BOX at the bottom centre, a rounded rectangle 560 by 80 px at x 448 to 1008, y 690 to 770, outline teal #0072B2, containing the text 3 kg 600 g (44 px, bold, dark). EXTRA LABEL: the text 5 kg (36 px, bold, dark #1F2937) at (683, 214), just left of the 0 at the top (the full turn is 5 kg). COUNT MARKS: on the arc between the 3 kg label (mark 15) and the needle (mark 18), three small teal #0072B2 dots (12 px) sit on marks 16, 17 and 18, with the small text 1, 2, 3 (28 px, teal) just outside the dial next to each dot. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any count of marks that differs from 25 (5 gaps between each pair of labels), or a long mark that is not at 0, 1 kg, 2 kg, 3 kg or 4 kg
a needle that is not on the 18th mark, or more than one needle
any label other than 0, 1 kg, 2 kg, 3 kg, 4 kg and 5 kg on the face
images.takeaway: Start at 0, find the last label the needle has passed, then count the small marks after it: 3 kg and 3 marks of 200 g is 3 kg 600 g.
images.description: A round scale with a 5 kg full turn and the needle three marks past the 3 kg label, reading 3 kg 600 g.
images.context: Concept image for Reading a Scale With a Needle. It follows the idea of the scales in your maths book (0 at the top, labels, small marks and a needle) and shows the concept's own example (practice values).
images.teaching_notes: Trace the face clockwise from 0 with a finger, stop at the last label passed, then count the marks. The slip to watch: reading the nearest label and ignoring the marks.

image_decisions.why: The scale with its three counted marks shows that the needle's position is read as the last label plus counted marks.
